title: Representative Success and Failure Case Analysis
purpose: Illustrate quantitatively predefined representative success and failure patterns of the frozen end-to-end pipeline at the patient level.

A_B.role: Largest segmentation-induced EF error and most confident misclassification

main_findings: A large segmentation-associated EF propagation error can coincide with an incorrect EF-band prediction even when classifier confidence is high.
Large end-to-end EF disagreement may arise substantially from disagreement between reference EF and the selected 2D geometry-based measurement method rather than from segmentation alone.
Small continuous EF differences can alter categorical EF-band assignment when the reference lies near a predefined class boundary.
A representative successful case showed that strong segmentation, small quantitative disagreement, and correct classification can align within the frozen pipeline.
limitations: Representative cases are illustrative and do not estimate the prevalence of each failure mechanism.
Historical prediction masks were not retained; regenerated masks are therefore restricted to qualitative visualization.
A small discrepancy remained between regenerated masks and stored historical Dice metrics.
The exact implementation-level source of the small reproduction discrepancy was not recoverable from the retained experiment records.
Observed upstream-downstream error associations should not be interpreted as proof of causality.
Classifier confidence scores are uncalibrated and should not be interpreted as calibrated probabilities or patient-level reliability guarantees.
